note: v1, written: NIGHT FREIGHT. Instrumental post-metal (the style board's t3 row): a freight train crosses the album at night, and the wheels' clack over the rail joints becomes the riff's odd meter. 132 bpm, B minor in drop-tuned guitars. 7/8 (the wheels) against 4/4 (the crescendo). Seven movements, 8:10. I CROSSING: a level-crossing bell; the freight's rumble swells; synthesised wheel clacks rise on a 14-sixteenth cycle; the horn's three tones drop a semitone as it passes. II JOINTS: a clean 8-string arpeggio riff of seven eighths (2+2+3) on the clack rhythm, fretless bass, rims, then toms. III CHUG: the riff drop-tuned on doubled m8 rigs (palm-muted 16ths into an open power chord), fuzz bass, sub, a room kit with ride; a tremolo-picked lead plays THE LINE. IV YARD: the train gone; wind, distant metal in a 6 s yard hall every 5 bars, a cello drone, the ebow sings THE LINE augmented. V CLIMB: 4/4 - the clean riff stretched to eight eighths over growing toms, the bass walking the riff inverted, then tremolo walls (power chords picked in 16ths) and the ebow an octave up, the kit to full. VI DERAILED: half-time doom in A (A C Bb | A G | C Bb | G A), china, sub, and the wheels' 7 back against the 4. VII LAST CAR: the clean riff alone with the bell, the horn far away and lower, the clacks fading, wind. note: v2, written: FREIGHT BY SEA, and the movements develop. (1) Off the rails: The Last Train (t6) is built on a synthesised train too, so trains are chirper-three's. Night Freight moves to a container port at night. A gantry crane's chain clanking through its sheave keeps the 14-sixteenth cycle and the riff's 7/8; a buoy bell is struck by the swell at irregular gaps; waves; a ship's diesel throbs (brown noise and a 46 Hz hum under a 2.7 Hz tremolo); the foghorn sounds two low tones (B, F#); the yard becomes the container stacks: containers set down, air brakes, a reversing alarm far off. (2) THE OPERATOR, the album's synthesised speech done small and close: a crane operator on a handheld intercom (voice-speech, ARPAbet, walkie-talkie band and drive), "seven, clear to lift" (the seven is the meter), "lowering", "hold"; at the end "last one, lights stay on". (3) No looping: the 64-bar chug runs in four stages: the riff; its grouping rotated 3+2+2; THE LINE over it; stabs on every group over double kick, and a one-stab break into the stacks. A second guitar's natural harmonics answer the clean riff in the joints. The undertow's doom thins in its last 8 bars to one held A chord every two bars, with an ebow crying A-G-E. note: v3, written: THE LIFT and THE DRUMMER. The climb's last 16 bars, the full kit with tremolo walls, go up a whole tone into C#, the ebow's line with them, so the undertow's fall to A lands a major third down instead of a tone. The kit learns a vocabulary: tom fills (t1 t1 t2 t2 t3 t3 ft ft, rising) on the last half-bar of every 8-bar phrase in the chug, the climb and the undertow, and snare rolls swelling into the chug and into the climb's full kit. A phrase's end is now heard as a drummer's decision, not a loop point. Reverse-cymbal swells are drawn into the chug, the climb's full kit, the undertow and the last ship. compscore seeds 0/11/19/29: v2 93.855/93.931/93.912/93.910 -> v3 94.029/94.040/94.052/94.041 (spectrum 94.4-95.1 -> 95.8-96.0). note: v4, written: THE PORT TELLS ITS STORY. The operator's words now move the crane: after "seven, clear to lift" a hoist motor whines upward far across the stacks (a pitch riser band-passed at 1 kHz into the 6 s yard hall, about 12 dB under the music); after "lowering" it falls away and a container lands far off (floor tom and crash bell); the second "clear" lifts again. Two ships: the foghorn (B, F#) is answered from further out (A, E, lower, darker, wetter), once on the quayside and once, softer, in the last ship. The crane winds down: in the last ship the chain's clank cycle stretches (14 ... 18, 20, 22, 24, 28, 34, 42 sixteenths), each pair softer, and stops under the clean riff. The 7/8 that started the piece slows to nothing before the end. compscore seeds 0/11/19/29 under the album's new measures (recurrence band 0.25-0.9, rhythm weight 0.03; v3 re-measured like for like): v3 97.260/97.272/97.281/97.276 -> v4 97.280/97.291/97.302/97.298.
